title: Why a relay beats manual-entry factors
desc: Three parties: the user, an impostor verifier, and the real verifier. The user types a one-time code into the impostor, which relays the output to the real verifier. The real site returns a session cookie that the relay sees. A note says manual-entry authenticators such as OTP and out-of-band codes are never phishing-resistant, because an impostor can relay the output to the real verifier. A final note says that with a passkey, a page on another domain can neither request your RP ID nor get a signature for it.
